definitions.explanation: A polite word for a notice, announcement, or piece of information communicated to someone. The honorific prefix お makes it suitable for formal and everyday use.

examples.japanese: お{知|し}らせ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧。
⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧なお{知|し}らせです⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧お⟦{読|よ}み→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: This is an important notice, so please read it carefully.

examples.japanese: ⟦{休業|きゅうぎょう}→休業：11541_kyuugyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧お{知|し}らせ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{入|い}り{口|ぐち}→入り口：02507_iriguchi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{貼|は}ってあった→貼る：10447_haru⟧。
examples.english: A notice about the closure was posted at the entrance of the shop.

notes: Ubiquitous in daily life — seen on websites, in emails, on signs, and in apps. Common patterns include ～⟦の→の：09472_no⟧お{知|し}らせ (notice about ~) and お{知|し}らせ⟦いたします→いたす：01314_itasu⟧ (we would like to inform you). Without the お prefix, ⟦{知|し}らせ→知らせ：03252_shirase⟧ is a plain noun meaning news or information. The phrase ⟦{嬉|うれ}しい→嬉しい：00822_ureshii⟧お{知|し}らせ (happy news) and ⟦{悲|かな}しい→悲しい：00783_kanashii⟧お{知|し}らせ (sad news) are set expressions for delivering good or bad news.
